cards.title: The US in Brief: Huang and Lutnick called to testify
cards.preview: Friday’s newsletter reports Senate demands for testimony from Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick over Nvidia and chip-export oversight. Its related analysis examines the leadership challenge facing Nvidia after Huang’s departure.
cards.durationBasis: Rough planning allowance for the linked analysis; not a measured article runtime

cards.title: Why you should expect an AI crash
cards.preview: This week’s cover newsletter weighs the AI investment boom against historical technology bubbles and doubts about future revenues. Its central distinction is that an AI bust looks likely without necessarily producing a wider financial catastrophe.
cards.durationBasis: Rough planning allowance for the linked analysis; not a measured article runtime

cards.title: The US in Brief: A historic Democratic win in Mississippi
cards.preview: Thursday’s US round-up leads with Scott Colom’s narrow Senate victory in Mississippi and the changing political map of the South. It also examines scrutiny of Nvidia and the administration; the linked leader argues for a change at the company’s top.
cards.durationBasis: Rough planning allowance for the linked analysis; not a measured article runtime

cards.title: The Insider: Are we on the cusp of an AI market bust?
cards.preview: The Insider asks whether rapid technical progress can justify AI valuations and the scale of investment in data centres. The discussion contrasts earlier technology busts with today’s geopolitical risks, retail-investor exposure and potential knock-on effects of disappointing revenues.

cards.title: The US in Brief: Pete Hegseth will fight another day
cards.preview: Wednesday’s newsletter reports the procedural move that stalled Pete Hegseth’s impeachment and Jim Jordan’s selection as the next House Republican leader. Its related economic analysis asks whether divided government will bring compromise or gridlock for Trumponomics.
cards.durationBasis: Rough planning allowance for the linked analysis; not a measured article runtime

cards.title: The US in Brief: Wealth tax fails in California
cards.preview: Tuesday’s round-up leads with California voters rejecting a proposed one-off wealth tax on billionaires. It also follows renewed impeachment articles against Pete Hegseth; the linked War Room analysis considers the pressure on his position.
cards.durationBasis: Rough planning allowance for the linked analysis; not a measured article runtime

cards.title: Inside Defence: What’s next for Ukraine?
cards.preview: Inside Defence questions whether ‘stalemate’ accurately describes Ukraine’s war, examining battlefield adaptations, strikes on energy infrastructure and outside leverage. The briefing also considers why a political settlement remains difficult despite renewed diplomacy.
cards.durationBasis: 37-minute recording stated in the later Insider newsletter; same canonical episode URL

cards.title: The US in Brief: A “hard yes” on impeaching Hegseth
cards.preview: Monday’s newsletter covers growing support for impeaching Pete Hegseth and the obstacles to a Senate conviction. It also looks at Nithya Raman’s victory in Los Angeles; the related analysis explores what the city can expect from its new mayor.
cards.durationBasis: Rough planning allowance for the linked analysis; not a measured article runtime

cards.title: Nannying for the ultra-rich is increasingly lucrative
cards.preview: The Saturday newsletter describes the growing market for rota-nannies serving ultra-wealthy families. Alternating teams offer round-the-clock care and high pay, but the arrangement also raises questions about demanding work and avoiding burnout.
cards.durationBasis: Rough planning allowance for the linked analysis; not a measured article runtime
